P0200.d: P0200 is the injector circuit fault without a cylinder assignment. The large US manufacturers do not use it – GM and Ford report injector faults per cylinder (P0201 ff) or as faults of the shared injector supply (P062D/P062E, P2146 ff).
s: Engine does not start or shuts down
c: Shared injector supply open (fuse, relay, harness connector)
Separate injector power stage or its wiring faulty (diesel)
Driver stage in the engine module faulty
Ground fault of the module or power stage

P0201.d: P0201 reports an electrical fault, mainly an open circuit, in the injector circuit of cylinder 1. The engine module watches each injector output: GM flags an open circuit at an impedance of 200 kΩ or more – on direct injection and diesel engines in 10 of 20 or 5 of 10 samples and with the warning light in the first trip, on some port-injected engines only after two trips.
s: Misfire and rough running, misfire code P0301
Limp mode possible on diesel and direct injection
c: Connector at the cylinder 1 injector loose, corroded or with a broken or pushed-back pin
Wire between module and injector open or chafed (heat, rodents)
Injector supply missing (fuse, relay) – then usually several cylinders at once
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

Leaking valve: hot-start problems, flooding, black smoke
c: Connector or wire corroded or open
Valve coil open or valve stuck
Thermo-time switch or control relay faulty
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

P0215.d: The engine shutoff solenoid is the electric stop valve on older diesel injection pumps, mainly distributor pumps. It is energised with the ignition on and lets fuel into the pump; with no current a spring closes it, the pump runs dry and the engine stops – also as a safety backup if the governor fails.
s: Engine does not start or stalls while driving
Engine keeps running after ignition off (solenoid stuck open)
c: Shutoff solenoid faulty (open coil, sticking plunger)
Relay or fuse in the supply circuit faulty
Broken wire, corrosion or ground fault at the pump connector

P0216.d: P0216 is a diesel code for the control of injection timing. On 1990s distributor pumps with an electronic timing advance it meant that actual injection timing missed its target; today manufacturers use it for the electronic injector control, with different meanings.
s: Hard starting or stalling (distributor pump), smoke
c: Injector harness or connector (broken pin) – common rail
Engine module or injector power stage faulty internally
Distributor pump electronics or timing advance faulty
Low supply pressure on distributor pumps (lift pump, filter)
Pump installed incorrectly, drive gear misaligned

P0217.d: P0217 is a condition code: the engine module reports that coolant temperature has passed a protection threshold. The limit and the reaction depend on the manufacturer – Saab's 2.2 diesel sets it at 120 °C for over 10 s, limits fuel quantity and suspends EGR and boost diagnostics until the temperature drops; heavy-duty diesels cut power sharply and may shut down; Ford petrol engines use their own code P1299 and cut fu
s: Temperature gauge in the red, overheat warning
Loss of power, limp mode, cylinders possibly shut off
Steam or coolant smell, coolant loss
c: Radiator fan, fan clutch or water pump faulty, radiator clogged
Coolant temperature sensor or harness faulty (false reading)
Extreme load (towing, gradient, heat) with an intact cooling system

P0218.d: P0218 is a condition code: the transmission or engine module reports that transmission fluid temperature sensor A reads above an overheat limit. Saab's Aisin automatic sets it above 170 °C for more than 10 s, or above 140 °C for two minutes at high speed, shows a 'transmission overheating' warning and shifts less smoothly; afterwards a fluid change is advised because the additives are spent.
s: Limp mode or reduced power possible
c: High load (towing, hills, sustained full throttle, stop-and-go in heat)
Fluid cooler, thermostat or lines clogged, weak cooling system
Torque converter clutch slipping or internal damage
Temperature sensor or wiring reading wrongly

P0219.d: P0219 is a condition code: engine speed has exceeded the overspeed limit even though the rev limiter already cuts fuel – so the engine was driven from outside, usually by downshifting at too high a road speed or descending in too low a gear, or the speed signal was wrong. Limits: Ford 6.7 litre diesel above 4,200 rpm, 3.0 litre above 4,800 rpm, after 0.1 s; GM/Saab 2.8 V6 petrol with manual gearbox above 7,000 rpm fo
s: Usually no lasting symptoms, only a stored code
Briefly very high revs, limiter intervening
After real overspeed: rattling, loss of power
c: Downshift at too high a road speed (manual gearbox)
Descending in too low a gear
Fault in the speed signal (crankshaft sensor, wiring)
Diesel runaway (oil drawn into the intake) or sticking injection

P0230.d: The fuel pump circuit has two sides: the primary circuit is the engine module's output to the fuel pump relay coil (or to a pump control module), the secondary circuit is the power circuit from relay contact or module to the pump itself. P0230 concerns the primary side.
s: Engine cranks but does not start
No pump prime noise at ignition on; with a short to voltage the pump runs on and drains the battery
c: Fuel pump relay faulty (coil open or shorted)
Control wire from module to relay open or shorted to ground or voltage
Relay supply, ground or fuse missing
With a pump control module: its supply, ground or the module itself

P0231.d: The fuel pump circuit has two sides: the primary circuit is the engine module's output to the fuel pump relay coil (or to a pump control module), the secondary circuit is the power circuit from relay contact or module to the pump itself. P0231 means the secondary side reads low, and the meaning differs by system.
s: Engine cranks but does not start
c: Power wire from relay or module to pump shorted to ground (chafing at tank or underbody)
Relay contact not closing, fuse or battery feed to the relay missing
Pump motor jammed or shorted (high current)
Connector at the tank flange corroded or burnt

P0232.d: The fuel pump circuit has two sides: the primary circuit is the engine module's output to the fuel pump relay coil (or to a pump control module), the secondary circuit is the power circuit from relay contact or module to the pump itself. P0232 means there is voltage in the pump power circuit although the pump should be off – a welded relay contact or a power wire shorted to another supply.
s: Fuel pump keeps running after switch-off
Check engine light on (GM after two trips)
c: Pump power wire shorted to another supply
Pump control module output stage shorted
Moisture or corrosion in the connector causing leakage current

P0233.d: The fuel pump circuit has two sides: the primary circuit is the engine module's output to the fuel pump relay coil (or to a pump control module), the secondary circuit is the power circuit from relay contact or module to the pump itself. P0233 reports brief, recurring dropouts in the pump power circuit that count neither as steadily low nor high.
c: Loose contact at pump connector, tank flange or relay socket

P02CA.d: Turbocharger B is a second, separately controlled turbo – on twin-turbo or two-stage systems, or one per bank. No manufacturer using the turbo B codes was found; twin-turbo engines such as GM's 3.0 V6 and Ford's 3.5 EcoBoost report boost faults under P0234/P0299 with a shared boost sensor, so the description follows CARB and the turbo A codes.
s: Check engine light, reduced power, limp mode
c: Wastegate B stuck closed, linkage seized
Boost control valve or actuator B faulty, vacuum line swapped or leaking

P02EC.d: Ford's 6.7 and 3.0 diesels control the air mass through the EGR valve and the intake throttle. P02EC means the measured air mass stays above target with the control at its limit – too little EGR, or the throttle cannot restrict enough – for 10 s (6.7) or 5 s (3.0).
c: EGR valve stuck closed or EGR cooler clogged
Mass airflow sensor reading too high

P02ED.d: Ford's 6.7 and 3.0 diesels control the air mass through the EGR valve and the intake throttle. P02ED means the measured air mass stays below target with the control at its limit – too much EGR, a throttle stuck closed or a clogged intake – for 10 s (6.7) or 5 s (3.0).
s: Smoke, high soot load in the filter
c: Intake throttle stuck closed or coked
Mass airflow sensor reading too low (dirty)

Flap or shaft bent, stop worn, gear worn
Wrong or not learned replacement part

CARB lists such heated fuel preparation systems among the monitored output components.

Rough running right after a cold start
c: Coil of the cold-start injector or valve open
Connector loose, corroded or pin pushed back
Fuse or relay of the cold-start system
Driver stage in the engine module

P02FF.d: Many diagnostics need to know how long the engine – or, on hybrids, the whole propulsion system – has been off: thermostat and evaporative checks and the cold-start strategy, for which CARB requires at least 6 hours of standstill. A timer measures this time, and the engine module checks its plausibility, for example against coolant cooling – a GM patent describes such a check.
s: Check engine light on, otherwise usually nothing noticeable
Clock in the instrument cluster wrong or reset
c: Time source in another module (instrument cluster, body module) gives an implausible time after a reset or voltage loss
Software level of engine, transmission or instrument cluster module
Battery discharged or disconnected, voltage dips
Instrument cluster or timer in the engine module faulty
Coolant temperature sensor distorting the cooling check
